COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB65 (2026-08-18): ONE screen (DataBinder.ScreenRepositoryIntrinsicName) asked by every declaration funnel — data-name, condition-name, index-name, file-name, paragraph/section name — rejects (COBOLNET1649) a user-defined word spelling an intrinsic-function-name the REPOSITORY identifies (FUNCTION name INTRINSIC, or every catalogued name under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC); LENGTH/RANDOM/SIGN/SUM are reserved words already. A catalogued name the REPOSITORY does not identify stays a legal user-defined word (SQRT as a table, MOD as an item — the golden's control) and its FUNCTION-less spelling a data reference. Editions: the REPOSITORY function-specifier is 2002+ (85 has no REPOSITORY).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: The lexer's FLOAT_BODY (and its DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA twin FLOAT_COMMA_BODY, kb/Work PB98) is exactly the form — a fixed-point literal, the letter E without intervening spaces, a fixed-point exponent; the sign-adjacent twins (function-argument regions, SUBSCRIPT mode) keep -1.5E3 one token (kb/Work R17).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). 'shall include a decimal point' is the lexer's shape (a point-less 1E10 is a user-defined word, §8.3.1.1 — it is diagnosed as an undefined name, which it is); 'from 1 to 36 digits' is checked at the ONE normalizer both funnels share (COBOLNET1661 — a 40-digit significand); a 36-digit significand seeds a floating-point numeric-edited item exactly (the golden's E1).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). 'a maximum of four digits' — COBOLNET1661 for a fifth (1.0E12345, which used to reach Roslyn as an overflowing C# double literal, CS0594); the IMPLEMENTOR-DEFINED maximum / minimum exponent VALUE is documented in CONFORMANCE.md §7 A.1 item 82 and enforced at compile time: the binary64 range for a literal in a native arithmetic expression / statement (about 4.9E-324..1.8E+308 — 1.0E+400 / 1.0E-400 → 1661), decimal128's under STANDARD-DECIMAL (1.0E+400 / 1.0E+398 evaluates to 100), the receiver's binary form for a VALUE on a FLOAT-SHORT (binary32) / FLOAT-LONG (binary64) item (§13.18.63.3 SR2), and no bound beyond the receiver's PICTURE for a VALUE on a fixed-point or floating-point numeric-edited item (PIC 9E+9999 VALUE 1.0E+9999).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). A zero significand with a nonzero exponent (0.0E+5), a negative zero significand (-0.0E+0) or a negative-signed exponent (0.0E-0) is COBOLNET1661 — in a VALUE clause, a level-88 and a statement alike (the ONE normalizer).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). The literal's value — significand × 10^exponent — is carried EXACTLY wherever the standard's semantics are the value's: a VALUE clause (NumericLiteral.ExpandFloatingPoint for a fixed-point subject, EditComposeFloat for a floating-point numeric-edited one), an OPERAND position (a MOVE source, a relation / EVALUATE comparand, a PERFORM VARYING FROM / BY value, a function argument — NumericRenderer.LiteralOperandNum → CobolDec.FromParsed on the exact-decimal lane; before PB99 MOVE 1.2345678901234567890123E+3 stored 1234.56789012345685803008 and FROM 1.0E+3 set a 20-decimal item to 999.999…9161), and every position under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL (§8.8.1.5.2 r1). Inside a NATIVE arithmetic expression or statement the literal is a binary64 operand (numeric design D16 — §8.8.1.3's implementor-defined method; documented, CONFORMANCE.md §7 item 82).

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB71 (2026-08-18): literal-1 is an alphanumeric (plain or hexadecimal), boolean or national literal, or a concatenation of them - ONE grammar arm (ALL allLiteral), ONE constructor (BoundAllLiteral.Of - the category rides on literal-1's class through CobolLiteral.ClassOf), the & fold per 8.8.3.3 GR2; a zero-length literal-1 is COBOLNET1648 and a mixed-class concatenation COBOLNET1540 (the version pass); the national/boolean literal-1 is the COBOL-2002 introduction below 2002 (COBOLNET0900). Before: ALL N"..." had no grammar arm, ALL B"..." parsed and died at run time, VALUE refused NX"..."/BX"..." and every ALL literal (a raw-text classifier).

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): ALL symbolic-character-1 with an undeclared name is COBOLNET1670 citing this rule; a declared one substitutes (the golden's ALL-ZED line). The BARE form is a word reference — an undeclared word is the ordinary undefined-reference diagnostic.

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): the figurative fill — repeated character by character to the associated item's size, then right-truncated — over a VALUE clause (VAL-FILL3: position 3 of a PIC X(3) VALUE BELL holds the character) and a fixed-length MOVE receiver (MOVE-FILL: position 4 of an X(4)); the ALL-literal fill of PB71's golden is the same rule over a longer literal-1. One node (BoundAllLiteral) carries the semantics for the classic figuratives, ALL literal-1 and the symbolic characters alike.

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): where the context does not size the string — a) in a concatenation, one character (the ConcatFolder figurative arm); b) a figurative other than ALL literal-1, one character (the golden's STRING-SC line: a bare symbolic character contributes ONE character to STRING); c) ALL literal-1, the literal's length (PB71's golden).

subject: Function-identifier
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB61 — the LENGTH/BYTE-LENGTH folds enumerated from the rule branches; one builder for a runtime-length group; SR6 decided from the definition before binding). SR6 'if a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments' — decided ONCE, from the DEFINITION (the catalog signature, or a REPOSITORY user function's USING formals — SR6 names function-prototype-name-1 too) and BEFORE any argument binds, on every route: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (1:4) drew the §15.3 arity error (the empty list bound first; only RANDOM, MinArgs 0, reached the SR6 arm) and keyword-omitted UPPER-CASE (1:4) under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC died as 'not defined' (the MinArgs guard sent it to the data path). Now COBOLNET1543 (SR6/SR8) on all of them; ResultRefMod no longer carries an SR6 arm. Negatives pb61-sr6-function-keyword-refmod (85+), pb61-sr6-keyword-omitted-refmod and pb61-sr6-udf-prototype-refmod (2002+); FunctionRefModSr6SweepTests sweeps the CATALOG — every argument-permitting row in both forms draws 1543 (never 1504/1639), every zero-argument row (CURRENT-DATE (1:8), the standard's own D.14.3.6 shape) does not.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB70 (2026-08-18): the SR1 list is ONE exclusion rule (RefModExclusion) at bind - COBOLNET1647 for a strongly-typed or variable-length (8.5.1.12) group, a numeric item of a non-DISPLAY/NATIONAL usage, an edited/numeric leaf subordinate to a strongly-typed group, an index item, a pointer, an object reference; an admitted GROUP is viewed through its character image (GroupImagePlace). Residues: a numeric item of usage NATIONAL (admitted by SR1) has no national image channel yet (loud stage); bit and national GROUPS read as ordinary groups until GROUP-USAGE is modelled (PB79).

subject: Reference-modification
notes: The POSITIVE half (a function-identifier IS admissible as identifier-1) and the NEGATIVE half (it shall be an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function) are both enforced. Before fix-queue PB8 the shape was a COBOL0001 parse error at every edition, so neither half could be reached. A non-conforming class is rejected with COBOLNET1629; national and alphanumeric results are covered by the golden, and the user-defined-function result reference-modifies through RefModPlace using the RETURNING item's own category.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: Found unenforced by the PB8 sibling sweep, not by PB8's own repro: MOVE A (3:4)(2:2) COMPILED CLEAN and silently returned A(2:2), because dataReferenceSuffix* admits unlimited ref-mods and the resolver kept only the first of each carrier while the DEFAULT-mode form outranked the SUBSCRIPT-mode one. Now counted in ONE place per reference kind and rejected with COBOLNET1630. A subscript followed by a ref-mod (the legal 8.4.3.1.4 GR1 a-to-g order) is unaffected.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB73 (adjudicated 2026-08-18): leftmost-position is a boolean position for a boolean item — in EITHER form (GR5a makes the positions bits under USAGE BIT and characters otherwise): a BIT-form slice moves bits 2-3 into a boolean receiver (01) and INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(BB4(1:3)) = 5; a DISPLAY-form slice is the same class-boolean unique item over character positions (INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN(B4(2:3)) = 2). An alphanumeric position for an alphanumeric item; a national position for a national one.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB70 + PB73 (2026-08-18): a usage-DISPLAY item of a category other than alphanumeric is OPERATED UPON for reference modification as if redefined class-and-category alphanumeric of the same size — the rule governs the OPERATION (positions are the character positions of that redefinition: a numeric-DISPLAY item's digit/sign characters, an edited item's characters, an alphabetic or display-form boolean item's characters), while GR6 gives the RESULT its class and category (PB73 re-adjudicated PB72's reading, which had made every such view alphanumeric — the display-form boolean slice stays boolean and the alphabetic slice alphabetic). RefModPlace.CategoryOf is the ONE reader.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB70 + PB73 (2026-08-18): the unique data item is elementary, without JUSTIFIED, and has the same class, category, and usage as that DEFINED for identifier-1 except the EXHAUSTIVE list — (a) alphanumeric-edited → alphanumeric (the RB leg: an edited slice moves to a boolean receiver), (b) national-edited → national (a staged skeleton), (c) numeric / numeric-edited → national under a national usage, alphanumeric otherwise (RefModPlace.CategoryOf's one rewrite arm) — so a boolean slice (bit- or display-form) stays boolean and an alphabetic slice stays alphabetic (Table16Operand.Of(Place)'s rider); PB72's 2026-08-09 reading (every display-form view alphanumeric) is reversed by PB73. RefModPlace.Category is the ONE reader every consumer asks.

Arithmetic expressions
notes: CONFORMS as of 2026-08-03 (fix-queue PB28, landed this session). Rule 6 has three parts. r6a (zero base requires exponent > 0) and r6c (negative base requires an integer exponent) are mandatory 'shall' requirements setting EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION, Fatal in Table 14. BEFORE the fix the STANDARD-DECIMAL arm enforced both (CobolDec.Pow) and EVERY NATIVE arm enforced neither, so the same program answered differently depending only on whether an ARITHMETIC clause was present: 0 ** 0 returned 1 (IEEE's convention, not COBOL's) and -2 ** 0.5 returned 0 (Math.Pow yields NaN and the quantizer made it zero), both with an ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken. CheckPowRule6 now screens every native arm. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY REACHABLE COMBINATION, not sampled: native at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023, and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2023 - all five raise both legs and leave the receiver unmodified per SS14.7.5. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is loudly refused (COBOLNET0806), so that arm is unreachable rather than unverified. r6b ('if the evaluation yields both a positive and a negative real number, the value returned is the positive number') is a SELECTION rule, not a screen, and cannot arise here: both bodies (CobolIntrinsics.PowNativeInt / PowNativeReal and CobolDec.Pow) yield a single value. Checked in the same pass rather than left to be discovered as a fourth leg.

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB64 T5 (2026-08-19): a class condition whose alphabet-name-1 names an ALPHABET … IS LOCALE [locale-name] — of EITHER class (alphanumeric, or FOR NATIONAL) — is COBOLNET1669 locale-alphabet-not-a-charset: a LOCALE alphabet defines a collating sequence only (§12.3.7.4 GR7, Table 6), so it names no coded character set a class condition could test membership of. DataBinder.IsLocaleAlphabet is the ONE predicate; the same rule family (§12.3.7.3 SR16g / SR17d — the IN phrases of SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS and CLASS; §13.18.13.3 SR1/SR2 — CODE-SET) awaits those phrases binding at all (kb/Work PB110). Rule --check verified at 8.8.4.4.3 2).

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB109 (2026-08-19) — item a) LANDED (it was a loud staged value): the condition is true iff the content consists entirely of characters in the coded character set alphabet-name-1 identifies — STANDARD-1/2 the 128 ISO 646 characters (STD-ASCII yes / STD-ACCENT no / STD-SPACE yes — membership, not the letter rule), a literal-phrase alphabet the TOTAL native set (GR7 k4 — REV-ANY yes, deliberately), UCS-4/UTF-8 the scalar values (an unpaired surrogate fails), with GR1's zero-length-false and GR2's NOT (NOT-STD). Items b/c/d (PB64 T5), e (BOOLEAN), f (class-name), n (NUMERIC) are live. STILL MISSING — the float class conditions g)–m): FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO / FLOAT-INFINITY / FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER(-QUIET/-SIGNALING) / IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE / NEAREST-TO-ZERO have no binder arm (a loud parse/bind failure, never a wrong answer) — PARTIAL on those alone.

subject: OPTIONS paragraph
notes: LANDED 2026-08-17 (with PB60 / AR-15.67.3-5). The OPTIONS clauses of a source element apply to all contained source elements unless overridden by a clause in a contained element's own OPTIONS paragraph: OptionsBinder.Bind now takes the container's model as the BASELINE (InheritConfiguration hands it over) and applies the containee's clauses on top, clause by clause. Golden legs: ARITH (the inner program without OPTIONS inherits ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL — 2/7*7 = 2,000000 in SDIDI arithmetic where native gives 1,999999) and ARITH2 (a second inner program's own OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE. overrides — 1,999999). Below 2002 the paragraph is inert (the pass's introduction gate), so a contained program's baseline is simply its container's defaults there.

subject: Configuration section
notes: LANDED 2026-08-17 (with PB60 / AR-15.67.3-5). A CONFIGURATION SECTION in a program contained within another program is diagnosed — COBOLNET1643 (catalogued descriptor), at every edition (X3.23-1985 carried the same restriction; no Annex E change) — after which the section is still walked so a second diagnostic never masks this one; the container's configuration applies (GR-12.3.4-1). Before this the containee's own section was silently bound locally. Negative fixture tests/conformance/negative/config-section-in-contained-program (reject-at 85 2002 2014 2023).

subject: Configuration section
notes: LANDED 2026-08-17 (with PB60 / AR-15.67.3-5). The container's configuration section applies to each directly or indirectly contained program: DataBinder.InheritConfiguration copies the whole configuration-derived state (SPECIAL-NAMES — DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, CURRENCY SIGN, CLASS names, ALPHABETs, switch mnemonics and status condition-names; OBJECT-COMPUTER's PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE; SOURCE-COMPUTER's DEBUGGING MODE; the REPOSITORY function/intrinsic/property specifiers) into every containee before it binds; the device-name mnemonics (Format 4, DISPLAY UPON / ACCEPT FROM) were already inherited by MnemonicRegistry's enclosing-unit walk — a second, tree-walking mechanism for the same rule, correct today and noted for folding into InheritConfiguration when the environment division gets a bound model. Implicit entries (the implied CURRENCY SIGN '$', the native alphabet) inherit as the defaults. Goldens: the 2023 one (six SPECIAL-NAMES/OBJECT-COMPUTER legs through a contained program, plus OPTIONS) and the 85 one (the edition-invariant five).

subject: Exception conditions
notes: kb/Work PB77 + PB75 (2026-08-18): with checking for a fatal exception condition NOT enabled 'the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and how any receiving operands are affected'. COBOL.NET's determination for the arithmetic size error condition without a SIZE ERROR phrase (EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, §14.7.5 no-phrase rule 4; A.1 item 70): execution continues and the resultant identifier receives the LOW-ORDER digits of the result aligned at its scale (CobolNum.Store's high-order truncation), for EVERY value carrier — SDIDI (CobolDec.ToUnscaled, PB74), the native exact family (Rescaled's unchecked arm), a binary64 (ToScaledUnchecked / FromDouble's unchecked form — the exact decimal expansion past the Int128 carrier). A non-finite binary64 landing in a fixed-point receiver stores ZERO. An INTERMEDIATE that cannot be formed at all (a standard-decimal intermediate past decimal128, a native value past the Int128 escape boundary in a value-semantics position, an exponentiation-rule violation, a zero divisor) has no result: execution does NOT continue — the run unit terminates abnormally, exit 1, naming the condition (PB75; it used to be a raw CLR crash, exit 127). Documented on CONFORMANCE.md (the item-70 row).

Citation validated (--check 15.19.3 "The source-format shall be different from the destination-format" -> OK, rule 3). The source-format space is {ANY, ANUM, HEX, NAT} and the destination space is {ANUM, ANUM HEX, NAT, NAT HEX, BYTE}, so the only pairs that can be the SAME format are ANUM->ANUM and NAT->NAT with no HEX - which is exactly `(src==1 && dst==1 && !hex) || (src==3 && dst==3 && !hex)`. ANUM -> ANUM HEX must NOT be diagnosed and is not (15.19.4 NOTE 3 a depends on it, and the corpus golden AH=41 pins it). ANY and BYTE cannot appear on both sides; a bare HEX destination is not in the format and is rejected earlier by the pair check (verified: CONVERT(WS-A ANUM HEX) and CONVERT(WS-A HEX HEX) both -> COBOLNET1514 'not a valid source-format destination-format pair'). subject: DAY-OF-INTEGER function
notes: SUSTAINED; both halves of the rule independently re-verified. 'return d.Year * 1000L + d.DayOfYear;' places the Gregorian year in the YYYY positions and the ORDINAL day of that year in DDD — the §15.5.4 Julian date form ('The Julian date form is YYYYDDD, where YYYY represents the year and DDD represents the ordinal date within that year'). YYYY half: 1 -> 1601001 (epoch year), 3067671 -> 9999365 (terminal year), 143951 -> 1995046. DDD half, over the 62-value spec-computed sweep described in RV-15.24.4-1: the leap-day ordinal is counted (2000-02-29 -> 2000060) and 366-day years reach 366 (2000-12-31 -> 2000366), while the century non-leap years do not (1900-12-31 -> 1900365, 1700-03-01 -> 1700060 vs 2000-03-01 -> 2000061), so §15.5.1's Gregorian leap rule is honoured in the DDD positions and not merely in YYYY. Identical at --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. Coverage note (not a test-need for this row): the cited test's only DAY-OF-INTEGER expectation is 01601001, whose DDD is 001 — no on-disk spec-derived case reaches a leap-day or a three-digit ordinal, which is why the DDD half was checked by running rather than by trusting the suite.

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes: UPHELD after varying the RECEIVER as well as the argument. Repertoire appends exactly one character per input character (a substitution replaces, never expands or drops), so the returned string's length is always argument-1's character count, and under D-N1 one national position is one UTF-16 char and one usage-display position. RAN MYSELF at --std 2023: FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(PIC N(5))) -> 005; the same over a PIC N(3) containing a SUBSTITUTED U+4E16 -> 003, so substitution does not change the length; the ZERO-LENGTH national literal FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N"") -> LENGTH 000 and an all-space receiver, which is correct since 15.26.3 carries no zero-length-literal prohibition (its 15.66.3 r3 twin does); a SUPPLEMENTARY-plane national literal in a PIC N(2) -> LENGTH 002 and '??', consistent with the declared D-N1 one-code-unit-per-position model; a reference-modified argument N-SRC(1:3) -> 3; a national GROUP of two PIC N(2) items -> 4. notes: Verdict SURVIVES; the note is corrected and the SPEC BASIS the adjudicator missed is supplied. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'standard-binary arithmetic is in effect' -> OK (rule 2). THE PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER, re-verified by me on the built CLI: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode with COBOLNET0806 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL' - a HARD error at --std 2002 (alongside COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'), 2014 and 2023, and NOT downgradable by --permissive (2023 adds the COBOLNET0903 obsolescence warning and still errors). Nothing in the tree computes 14114126198520207781233383725636853 / (2 ** 112); CobolIntrinsics.E() is the only body and is Math.E in every mode. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and the standard's own Annex E remark records that it 'has not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider'. The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: the STANDARD-BINARY keyword of the ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only; the compiler's own edition gate agrees - 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode. The honest cover is a negative case pinning that FUNCTION E under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE; a mode-only rejection test that never names E would not cover this row.

notes: CONFIRMED NOT-IMPLEMENTED, independently re-verified. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r5 returns whole, including 'If argument-4 is specified, the magnitude of the value shall be less than or equal to 1439.' I re-ran the search rather than trusting the prior pass: `grep -rn 1439 src/ --include=*.cs | grep -v Generated/` returns NOTHING — not in the binder, not in the renderer, not in the runtime. Argument-4 flows `IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFormattedDatetime` -> `ArgInt(ic.Args[3])` -> `CobolDate.EmitFormatted`, which only ever computes `offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes); oh = (int)(offMag / 60); om = (int)(offMag % 60)`. Consequences, both silent: 2000 minutes renders offset-hours 33, violating §15.3.3.6.2 ('The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive'); 9999 minutes renders 166, so `oh.ToString("00")` emits three characters and the returned value grows past the width the format describes. §15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist for an out-of-range argument even though the VALUE is implementor-defined; it is never set. Because argument-4 may be an identifier or an expression this cannot be a compile-time check in general, but it is a one-line runtime guard beside the existing integer-date guard in `CobolDate.FormattedDatetime`. NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than DIVERGES because there is no implementation to diverge from. The identical rule text is §15.41.3 r4 for FORMATTED-TIME and is equally unimplemented (same sweep). subject: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE function
notes:
REFUTER PASS. VERDICT RETAINED AT DIVERGES, AND THE DEFECT IS WIDER THAN THE ADJUDICATOR RECORDED.

CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.48.3 "If argument-1 is a date format, the contents of argument-2 shall be a valid date in that format." -> OK (§15.48.3 4)). cite.py --check 15.3 "If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value" -> OK (§15.3 rule 14), and I read that paragraph IN FULL because it is what forecloses every escape from the finding below: "... results in an incorrect value for that argument OR FOR THE RETURNED VALUE according to the rules specified in the function definition ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist ... If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference."

THE VALIDATION ITSELF IS CORRECT and I re-read every leg: CobolDate#Analyze walks the tokenized format against the data, requiring each in-data separator ('-', ':', 'W', 'T', 'Z') to appear, rejecting a non-digit, a short field and any trailing character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1;`), and range-checking every subfield with per-digit narrowing - year 1601..9999 (§15.3.1.3/.5/.7, "greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999"), month 1..12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth, day-of-year against the leap year, week against LongIsoYear, weekday 1..7. I checked LongIsoYear against §15.3.1.7's OWN formulation (53 weeks "if the year subfield represents a common year and January 4 of that year falls on Sunday, or if the year subfield represents a leap year and January 4 of that year falls on a Saturday or Sunday") and derived that it is equivalent to ISO 8601's Jan-1-Thursday / leap-Wednesday rule, which is what ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear implements - so the week cap is right. A nonzero result becomes ExceptionState#ArgumentError, which I read: it sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 - exactly §15.3 rule 14's disposition.

⛔ CORRECTION - THE WEEK-DATE CRASH WINDOW IS TWO DAYS WIDE, NOT ONE. The adjudicator cited only "9999W527". I recomputed .NET's ISOWeek.ToDateTime arithmetic by hand: 9999-01-04 is a MONDAY, so correction = 1 + 3 = 4 and ordinal = 52*7 + d - 4 = 360 + d, evaluated as `new DateTime(9999,1,1).AddDays(ordinal - 1)` against a 365-DAY year. d=5 gives 9999-12-31 (integer date 3,067,671, the §15.5.2 maximum - CORRECT and, usefully, the exact boundary the landed FORMATTED-DATE row pins as "9999W525"); d=6 gives 10000-01-01 and d=7 gives 10000-01-02, BOTH past DateTime.MaxValue, and BOTH throw System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule passes for both: 9999 > 1600 and <= 9999; 9999 is a 52-week ISO year so week 52 is inside 01..52; day-of-week 6 and 7 are inside 1..7. So "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W526" AND "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W527" are both PERMISSIBLE DATA that abort the run unit with a raw CLR stack trace - neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition, where §15.3 rule 14 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result. The extended forms "YYYY-Www-D"/"9999-W52-6" and "9999-W52-7" fault identically (same Analyze leg).

CORROBORATION, NOT INHERITANCE: the landed AR-15.79.3-5 RAN this input against the sibling and its own sweep records `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` as verified crashing identically. I re-derived it here from the code and the calendar arithmetic, and extended it to d=6, which no prior record had.

ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX - bound-check the week-date reconstruction in Analyze. Do not count this row, AR-15.48.3-5 and AR-15.79.3-5 as three queue items. THE LOW BOUNDARY IS CLEAN and I checked it rather than assuming it: 1601-01-01 is a Monday and lies in ISO 1601-W01, so ISO 1601-W01-1 = 1601-01-01 = integer date 1, and no week date can underflow the epoch.

test-ref EMPTY: no test, golden or corpus program feeds this function an INVALID argument-2 at all, so neither the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION path nor the crash is pinned anywhere. EDITIONS from the standard (Annex E carries no occurrence of the name), not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.

notes: VERDICT UPHELD, on stronger evidence than the original, with one citation corrected. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. CONTINGENCY WORTH RECORDING: this rule governs which of the TIED arguments is returned; whether the tie is real is RV-15.59.4-1's question, and at the boundaries documented there the 'greatest value' premise is itself wrong. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. REFUTER'S DECISIVE CASE - an equal-value tie between DIFFERENT contents, on the non-identity-PCS weights overload: E:/Temp/rfmax/tiew.cob (RFMAXTIEW) `OBJECT-COMPUTER. The reversal ITSELF is exactly right - CobolIntrinsics.Reverse is a position-j <- position-(n-j+1) code-unit reversal with no length change, fed the operand's FULL fixed-width image, and re-verified live at every shape tried: X(6) VALUE "AB" -> [    BA  ] into X(8) (n = the declared width, not the trimmed value); ref-mod W-S(2:3) -> [  B     ]; A(5) -> [EDCBA   ]; N(5) -> [EDCBA   ]; numeric-edited ZZ9 VALUE 42 -> [24      ] (the EDITED image is reversed, correct); alphanumeric-edited XXBXX "AB CD" -> [DC BA   ]; an image-capable group -> [EDCBA   ]. Surrogates need no special handling - 8.5.1.4 item 2 and its closing paragraph ('Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character', cite-checked) make code-unit reversal the spec-mandated behaviour. BUT THREE LEGAL argument-1 SHAPES PRODUCE NO RETURNED VALUE AT ALL - each compiles clean at 85 and 2023 and then throws CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at RUN time, where 15.78.4 r1 requires a character string of length n: (1) an alphanumeric GROUP item containing a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf - `01 G2. 05 G2-A PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC". 05 G2-N PIC S9(4) COMP-5 VALUE 5.` then `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(G2) TO W-X.` -> 'whole-group image of G2 with a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf - the Tier-C byte island'; the argument is legal because 8.5.2.1 makes an alphanumeric group item class AND category alphanumeric, which 15.78.3 r1 admits. (2) a FIGURATIVE CONSTANT - `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(SPACE) TO W-X.` -> 'intrinsic string argument BoundFigurative' (IntrinsicRenderer.StrArgVisitor.Visit(BoundFigurative) is a Loud arm); legal because 8.4.3.2.3 SR8 admits a literal, 8.3.3.6.4 GR1 makes SPACE an alphanumeric character value and GR3b fixes its length at one character position - exactly satisfying 15.78.3 r1. (3) `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(ALL "AB") TO W-X.` -> 'intrinsic string argument BoundAllLiteral' (the sibling Loud arm); 8.3.3.6.4 GR3c gives it the length of literal-1. The failures are LOUD, not wrong values, and the Tier-C group island is a general deferral (COBOLNET_DESIGN 4.2) rather than a REVERSE-specific bug - but it is NOT recorded in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (grep found no Tier-C / whole-group-image entry), so it is an open GAP, not documented non-support. Fixing StrArgVisitor's two Loud arms is the cheap half and closes the same hole for UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE/TRIM/CONCAT. TEST-REF STRUCK: `conformance:negative/reverse_national_result_to_an` was cited for this rule but does not cover it - it is a `*> reject-at: 2002 2014 2023` COMPILE-REJECT case for the 15.78.1 result-type table and the 14.9.25.3 Table 16 National->AN MOVE guard (CA25); the program never executes, so it cannot exercise a position-reversal rule. The surviving refs do exercise it (StringFamily_PinnedToSpec pins REVERSE("abc 12") -> [21 cba  ] against the SPEC; IF134A checks `IF FUNCTION REVERSE("CAPS") = "SPAC"`; ChannelMatrix reverses "ABCDE", though only differentially against the frozen legacy oracle). Test-needed: goldens for the group, figurative and ALL-literal shapes. subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: A combined WEEK-date-and-time format whose argument-2 is VALID per §15.3.1.7 aborts the run unit with an unhandled .NET exception instead of returning a value. `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYWwwDThhmmss", "9999W527T235959") TO WS-F.` at --std 2014 → 'Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException … at System.Globalization.ISOWeek.ToDateTime … at CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Analyze'. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Sibling sweep (same Analyze line, both verified crashing identically): `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` and `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` — the latter is the worse one, since §15.92 defines TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME as the VALIDATOR that returns an error position and can therefore never legitimately fault. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.

subject: SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT function
notes: §15.5.5: a standard numeric time form value is 'a numeric value representing seconds past midnight', and with LEAP-SECOND OFF in effect (the only supported mode; §7.3.17.4 GR1 implies OFF when unspecified) it 'shall be greater than or equal to zero and less than 86,400'. The runtime returns DateTime.TimeOfDay.Ticks — always in [0, 864,000,000,000) — and the renderer types it as NumX at scale 7, so the delivered numeric value is seconds in [0, 86400) with 7 fraction digits; function type Numeric per the catalog (§15.80.1 'The type of this function is numeric'). Both range endpoints are pinned (0 at midnight; 863,999,999,999 at 23:59:59.9999999), and the golden probes the range end-to-end through COMPUTE into PIC 9(5)V9(7).

subject: SIN function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.82.4 'The returned value is the approximation of the sine of argument-1 and is greater than or equal to' -> OK (rule 1). Implementation: CobolIntrinsics.Sin(double x) => Math.Sin(x), reached through RenderFloat (the catalog row is Float:true). Both halves of the rule verified: (a) approximation - Math.Sin is the binary64 sine with full argument reduction, and S15.82.4 specifies no equivalent arithmetic expression, so per S15.4.1 the approximation is implementor-defined in EVERY arithmetic mode (native: 'the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor'; the standard-mode returned-value-shall-equal-the-EAE requirement applies only 'when ... an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified', which is why SIN is correctly absent from the ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic loud-stage list); (b) range - Math.Sin returns a value in [-1,+1] for every finite double argument. Receiver handling preserves the bound: a FLOAT or receiverless context keeps the binary64 value through RealResult (NaN - reachable only from a non-finite COMP-2 argument - is screened to the S15.3 EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION default 0 or the raise under checking); a FIXED-POINT receiver quantizes through the one FromDouble at FloatWorkingScale >= 9, and rounding a |v| <= 1 value at scale >= 9 can produce at most exactly +/-1.0, still within the rule's bounds. Untested by a spec-derived test: IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests (GnuCOBOL differential) and NIST IF135A pin values but are regression nets - CONFORMS-but-untested.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED BY REVIEW (scripts/render-spec-page.py 935 = printed folio 905): the diagram is exactly `FUNCTION RANDOM [ ( [ argument-1 ] ) ]`, FUNCTION and RANDOM underlined, BOTH bracket levels present — the specs/ISO_COBOL.md transcription is faithful, no OCR over-restriction. RPAREN)?` admits all three shapes; the catalog row RANDOM/OptionalTrailing/MinArgs 0/MaxArgs 1 plus the BindIntrinsicCore arity check bound it. subject: RANGE function

subject: REM function
notes: Re-verified independently. TRANSCRIPTION: the canonical PDF's own text layer for printed folio 907 (PDF page 937) reads exactly 'FUNCTION REM ( argument-1  argument-2 )' -- nothing bracketed, no choice indicator, no ellipsis; the 300-dpi figure check already on record in docs/rearchitecture/spec-reconciliation/agents/compare-p933-p944.json covers 15.77.2 and found no lost delimiters, and the once-missing <u> markup (LEDGER.json systemic chapter-15 defect, REM named) is present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md today. GRAMMAR/BINDER: functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? literally present; the catalog Build row pins IntrinsicArity.Fixed 2..2. Verified by RUNNING the built compiler: the printed SPACE-separated form FUNCTION REM(A B), the 8.3.5 comma form, the 8.4.3.2 SR6 space-before-paren form FUNCTION REM (A B), an arithmetic-expression argument, a nested FUNCTION REM argument, and the adjacent-sign two-argument form FUNCTION REM(A -4) (= REM(11,-4) = 3, not a subtraction) all compile and give the ISO 15.77.4 values in argument order; FUNCTION REM(5) and FUNCTION REM(5 3 2) are both rejected with COBOLNET1504. Coverage caveat (not a downgrade -- a comma IS the 8.3.5 separator form of the printed space): both test-refs use only the comma form, so no committed test pins the printed space-separator spelling.

subject: REVERSE function
notes:
Printed folio 908 (PDF page 938) re-rendered and read independently: the format is `FUNCTION REVERSE ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and REVERSE both UNDERLINED (required), one unbracketed required operand, no optional phrase. Grammar: functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? ; REVERSE is NOT a lexer token (only REVERSE_VIDEO and REVERSED are - grep-verified over Grammar/) so it arrives as IDENTIFIER through functionName. The catalog row is Fixed 1..1 and the arity gate was re-run live against the built CLI: `FUNCTION REVERSE` (no parens) -> COBOLNET1504 '1 argument(s); 0 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE()` -> COBOLNET1504 '0 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE(W-A W-B)` -> COBOLNET1504 '2 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE(OMITTED)` -> COBOLNET1544 (8.4.3.2.3 SR7, cite-checked). The parens being syntactically optional in the grammar is harmless: the shape is still REJECTED, at bind time rather than parse time. ⚠ TRANSCRIPTION DEFECT (the prior draft asserted 'the transcription is faithful' - that claim is WITHDRAWN as false): specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.78.2 renders the general format as BARE MARKDOWN TEXT, with no 
 wrapper and no  markup, while every neighbour checked (15.75.2 RANDOM, 15.76.2 RANGE, 15.77.2 REM, 15.79.2 SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, 15.80.2 SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT) carries both. The required-word underlining the printed page shows is therefore LOST in the transcription. The verdict is unaffected - this format has no optional element, so nothing required-vs-optional turns on the underlining, and the compiler requires both words - but the defect is real and propagating: the Phase-B extractor's rule text for FMT-15.78.2 swallowed the trailing `` anchor precisely BECAUSE there is no 
 block to bound it. Repair 15.78.2 to the 
/ form of its neighbours. ⚠ Test coverage is POSITIVE-ONLY: both test-refs write the correct one-argument format (StringFamily_PinnedToSpec has an InlineData `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE("abc 12") TO T.`; IF134A carries 109 REVERSE references, e.g. `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE("figure") TO WS-ANUM.`), so acceptance is pinned, but NO test pins the four rejection shapes above - they were verified by hand. A negative golden for arity 0/2 and OMITTED is test-needed.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: PDF page 939 (printed folio 909) was RE-RENDERED independently for this review and the transcription is faithful: FUNCTION and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME are underlined (required words), argument-1 and argument-2 appear unbracketed inside the parentheses separated by a space — exactly two mandatory arguments, no optional phrase, no OCR-induced over-restriction. The grammar is the intended superset (`functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?`; the hyphenated name arrives as IDENTIFIER; arguments juxtapose or take the §8.3.5 comma separator), narrowed at bind time by the catalog row (IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2). Re-verified at --std 2014: the space-separated two-argument form compiles and returns +45296.00; one argument → COBOLNET1504 'takes 2 argument(s); 1 given (ISO §15.3)'; three arguments → the same 1504 with '3 given'; --std 2002 → COBOLNET1502 'introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2014'. The two test-refs write the general format's exact shape and assert a correct value, so they cover the positive side; the COBOLNET1504 arity rejection has no negative test.

subject: SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT function
notes: Format is the two required words FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT, no argument list (§15.80.2, both underlined). The functionCall alternative `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` parses the bare form; the catalog row (Fixed arity 0..0, IntrinsicBind.Runtime) makes any written argument draw COBOLNET1504 in the generic arity check, and the keyword-omitted bare name without a REPOSITORY declaration draws COBOLNET1543 per §8.4.3.2.3 SR2. `FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT ()` is accepted deliberately — the §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 NOTE's own empty-parens shape (`FUNCTION RANDOM ()`), not a leniency. A trailing `(1:5)` binds as a ref-mod of the RESULT (zero-argument function; the SR6 catalog half lives in ResultRefMod). Below --std 2014 the reference draws COBOLNET1502 (constructs.json row `seconds-past-midnight-2014`). Editions derived from the WG4 CD 1.2 (2009) Annex D.2 item 4 new-function list (kb/Work R28, adversarially verified 2026-08-08), not from the catalog row.

subject: SIGN function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py OK on §15.81.2 '( argument-1 )' — the general format is the one-line 'FUNCTION SIGN ( argument-1 )' with both words required and no optional bracket, so the historically lossy-diagram risk does not arise. Grammar: functionCall alt 1 'FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*' with SIGN listed in functionName (SIGN lexes as a reserved token and must be admitted explicitly); the parse is a deliberate superset (argument group optional) and BindIntrinsicCore enforces the exact arity from the catalog row (Fixed 1..1) with COBOLNET1504, so FUNCTION SIGN with zero or two arguments is rejected at bind with the §15.3 citation. The §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 keyword-omitted form (cite.py OK: 'the word FUNCTION may be omitted') is carried by the separate reservedIntrinsicArgFn alternative (PB9, kb/Work/PB9.md status landed) whose argument group is structurally REQUIRED — derived from §15.81.2 itself, which has no no-argument form — keeping the SIGN clause (§13.18.53) collision impossible; that form belongs to §8.4.3.2.3, not to this FMT rule, but the golden asserts both forms yield the same value. §8.4.3.2 SR6 paren discipline is honored via FNARG_LPAREN retyping (PB48). Test: pb9_reserved_intrinsic_names exercises FUNCTION SIGN(NEG) and SIGN(...) side by side with spec-derived expected values. Editions as for AR-15.81.3-1: introduced 2002, unchanged through 2023.

subject: SIN function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.82.2 '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>SIN</u> ( argument-1 )' -> OK. The format parses through functionCall's first alternative (FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? ...), SIN arriving as IDENTIFIER through functionName and resolving against the catalog row ("SIN", Numeric, Fixed, 1, 1, ..., IntrinsicBind.Runtime, Float:true). The diagram's required elements are all enforced: FUNCTION and SIN are required by the grammar alternative (SIN is not in reservedIntrinsicArgFn, so no keyword-omitted grammar form exists for it; the REPOSITORY omission is S8.4.3.2.3 SR2's separate allowance, handled by binder re-route); the parenthesized single argument is required at bind - the paren group is grammatically optional for zero-argument functions, and a bare FUNCTION SIN is rejected by the Fixed 1,1 arity check (COBOLNET1504), as is any second argument. The FNARG_LPAREN retyping implements S8.4.3.2.3 SR6 (the '(' after the name is always the argument list). Editions derived independently of the catalog row: SIN entered with the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment to COBOL-85 (it is exercised by the NIST CCVS-85 suite, IF135A) and appears in NO later-edition delta row of docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md (the 2023 seven-function delta, rows 65-73, does not include it), so it is present at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023. Untested by a spec-derived test: NIST IF135A/IF403M and IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests exercise the format but are regression nets - CONFORMS-but-untested.
